stem: External partners need to upload files over SFTP using their existing SFTP clients, and the team wants to avoid installing, patching, or operating any SFTP server software itself. Which service should the architect choose?

choices.text: A self-managed SFTP server running on an EC2 instance the team maintains
Amazon EFS mounted directly by each partner over the internet
AWS Transfer Family providing a managed SFTP endpoint in front of Amazon S3
Amazon S3 presigned URLs that the team generates individually and emails to each partner ahead of every upload

rationale: AWS Transfer Family is a fully managed SFTP, FTPS, FTP, or AS2 endpoint in front of S3 or EFS, so partners keep using their existing SFTP clients while the team runs no server infrastructure, matching the requirement exactly. A self-managed SFTP server on EC2 is precisely the server software the team said it wants to avoid installing, patching, and operating. Presigned URLs generated and emailed manually do not give partners an SFTP endpoint at all, and the manual distribution process does not match how the partners currently connect. Amazon EFS mounted directly by external partners over the internet is not how partners currently connect (over SFTP) and exposes a network filesystem to outside parties rather than a managed transfer endpoint.
